subject: mathematics
question_text: Prove that cosA · cos2A · cos4A · cos8A = sin16A / (16 sinA).

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.67 — SAQ chapter 10 T-Ratios upto Transformations, answer 69. Printed appearances: AP 17. The angles DOUBLE each time — A, 2A, 4A, 8A — and the answer is in 16A. That doubling chain is the whole method: each application of sin2θ = 2 sinθ cosθ moves one step up it. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — no [N Marks] tags are printed anywhere in this chapter (its pages are set two questions to a page in two columns). It is not a bare guess: the same book prints 1+1+1+1 for the 4-mark answers 58 and 59 on book p.63 and 1+2+1 for answer 61 on p.64, so both shapes used here are the book's own. The book's chapter header carries ★★ and reads '4 Marks'; that star is the CHAPTER's rank, not this question's. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7; Q14 is the T-Ratios slot. RE-CUT 2026-08-31: this card was filed as SAQ at 4 marks and is now VSAQ at 2. The original label came from the Baby Bullet-Q blueprint for the superseded 75-mark paper; the Sri Chaitanya FAST TRACK IPE Mathematics-IA 2026-27 edition files this chapter under a Very Short Answer Questions banner and prints no short answer block for it at all, asking this same question as Very Short Answer question 38. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The mathematics and the steps are unchanged; only the mark scheme moved: the two marks now sit on the step that manufactures the sine and on the doubling chain, and the closing line is a restatement that carries none. recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each move in order.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Multiply and divide by 2⁴ sinA
steps.margin_note: First mark, and the trick of the question. There is no sinA on the left, so one is introduced deliberately — multiplied AND divided, which changes nothing.
lines: = (2⁴ sinA)/(2⁴ sinA) · cosA cos2A cos4A cos8A
= (1/(16 sinA)) (2 sinA cosA)(2 cos2A)(2 cos4A)(2 cos8A)

recall.must_convey: That 2⁴ sinA is introduced by multiplying and dividing, so a sinA is available to start the doubling chain.
accept: multiply and divide by sixteen sin A so a sine appears to start the chain
introduce two to the fourth sin A top and bottom
bring in a sin A so the double angle formula can be used
sixteen sin A tho multiply and divide cheyyali
manufacture a sine to begin with

steps.why: sin2θ = 2 sinθ cosθ needs a sine to pair with the cosine. There is none on the left, so one is manufactured — and dividing by the same thing keeps the value unchanged.
common_mistakes: Multiplying by sinA without dividing, which changes the expression.
Introducing only one 2 instead of four.
steps.memory_tip: There is no sinA on the left, so introduce one — multiplied AND divided, which changes nothing.

steps.label: Apply the double angle repeatedly
steps.margin_note: Last mark. Each 2 pairs with the sine just made and the next cosine, doubling the angle: A → 2A → 4A → 8A → 16A. Four applications, one per 2.

recall.must_convey: That sin2θ = 2 sinθ cosθ is applied four times in succession, doubling the angle each time up to sin16A.
accept: apply the double angle four times so the angle doubles each step up to sin sixteen A
each two pairs with the sine and the next cosine to double the angle
repeat the formula until you reach sin sixteen A
prathi sari angle double avthundi, sin sixteen A varaku
use two sin cos four times in a row

steps.why: Each step consumes one 2 and one cosine and doubles the angle. Four cosines means four 2s and four doublings — which is exactly why the denominator is 2⁴.
common_mistakes: Applying the formula to the wrong pair.
steps.memory_tip: sin2θ = 2 sinθ cosθ applied four times: sinA becomes sin2A, then sin4A, sin8A, sin16A.

steps.label: State the result
steps.margin_note: The chain ends at sin16A over the 16 sinA that was introduced at the start.

recall.must_convey: That the result is sin16A/(16 sinA).
accept: the answer is sin sixteen A over sixteen sin A
the chain ends at sin sixteen A over the sixteen sin A introduced
that gives the right hand side
sin sixteen A by sixteen sin A vasthundi
the final answer is sin sixteen A over sixteen sin A

steps.why: The 16 in the answer is the 2⁴ introduced at the start, and the sinA is the one introduced with it. Every factor put in at the start is still there in the final answer.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as a product.
steps.memory_tip: The 2⁴ in the denominator is the 16. Write the final identity out.

insider_note: Multiply and divide by 2⁴sinA so that each 2 sin·cos collapses into the next sine. The 16 in the answer IS that 2⁴, so it has to be introduced at the start, not found at the end.
